newsitem.title: USA: U.S. blames salmon impasse on Canada.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blames salmon impasse on Canada.

text.p: The United States on Monday blamed the impasse in salmon talks on Canada's refusal to conserve stocks.

"Agreement has not yet been reached. We believe it is because Canada has been unable to make or accept a proposal that meets the minimum requirements to conserve salmon stocks off the West Coast," John Dinger, a State Department spokesman, told reporters.
"To reach an agreement that does not conserve depleted stocks is simply not in either countries' interest," he said.

Dinger said the United States had "made a good faith effort" to find a solution and he asserted that if Canada had not broken off negotiations in May "an agreement could have been in place right now."

With the commercial fishing season set to open as early as next week, Dinger said he was unaware that the two sides had set a specific date to resume their talks. He said negotiators were holding consultations with their respective capitals.
U.S. President Bill Clinton and Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien discussed the issue during the Group of Seven industrialised countries summit in Denver over the weekend, he said.
Canada and the United States reached a stalemate on Friday in bitter talks aimed at resolving a dispute over how to divide the Pacific salmon catch.

"These are very tough issues with straightforward and severe, or important, financial implications for both sides," Dinger said. But he remained upbeat about the prospects for a deal, saying "We believe that if the Canadians join us in a good-faith effort and in a spirit of compromise, that we can come to a solution."
"I understand that the president and prime minister, when they spoke about this, declared their intention to bring that spirit of good will and compromise to the negotiations."

When a Canadian reporter said Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy had expressed little hope that Canada would return to the table, Dinger replied: "That's not my understanding of the conversations in Denver."

The two countries held three days of negotiations last week, their first on the salmon dispute since talks collapsed in acrimony a month before. They have squabbled for years over how to divide dwindling salmon stocks off the Pacific Northwest and several attempts at a settlement have failed.
